description: Gold-standard expert-annotated benchmark cases for Day 2, Day 3, and Day 4 Stage 5/6 evaluation. Includes ground-truth step divergence index, error taxonomy classification, and Marks Recovery ROI calibration across Calculus, Differential Equations, and Physics / Vector Calculus.

cases.subject: Calculus III
canonical_steps: u = x^2, dv = cos(x)dx => du = 2x dx, v = sin(x)
u2 = 2x, dv2 = sin(x)dx => v2 = -cos(x). Apply uv - \int v du with outer minus: - [ -2x cos(x) - \int -2cos(x) dx ]
student_steps: u = x^2, dv = cos(x)dx => du = 2x dx, v = sin(x)
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student successfully set up both stages of integration by parts. The divergence occurred in Step 3 when expanding nested negative signs: the outer minus in - [ -2x cos(x) ... ] was distributed to make +2x cos(x), but the second integral term inside the brackets was inverted incorrectly, and the integration constant (+ C) was omitted in the final answer.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: High exam recurrence (15% of Exam 2). Sign distribution errors in repeated parts are high-velocity fixes through targeted spot-the-bug bracket drills.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.topic: Method Selection: Substitution vs Arctan Standard Form
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student attempted u-substitution on 1/(1+x^2). In Step 2, the student pulled an expression containing the integration variable x outside the integral sign: (1/2x) \int (1/u) du. Variables cannot be treated as constants across the integration operator. The fundamental error was selecting u-substitution instead of recognizing standard inverse trigonometric form.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Method hesitation between algebraic substitution and standard trigonometric tables causes severe time leaks during exams. Decision flowcharts provide clear visual branching rules.

cases.subject: Calculus III
canonical_steps: Identify essential infinite discontinuity at x = 0
Split into improper limit integrals: lim_{t->0^-} \int_{-1}^t x^{-2} dx + lim_{s->0^+} \int_s^1 x^{-2} dx
Show both limits evaluate to \infty, therefore integral diverges
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student blindly applied the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus across a non-removable infinite discontinuity at x = 0 without checking domain continuity. The function 1/x^2 is strictly positive everywhere on its domain, yet the student obtained a negative area of -2, failing to execute basic sanity checking or split the integral at the singularity.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Conceptual barrier regarding domain continuity. A concrete physical metaphor (e.g., measuring bridge height over an infinite canyon) permanently cures blind FTC application.

cases.subject: Calculus III
canonical_steps: Divide entire equation by 2x to put in standard form: y' + (1/(2x))y = (1/2)x^2
Compute integrating factor I(x) = e^{\int (1/(2x))dx} = e^{(1/2)ln(x)} = \sqrt{x}
Multiply and integrate: \sqrt{x} y = \int (1/2)x^{5/2} dx = (1/7)x^{7/2} + C
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student failed to transform the differential equation into standard linear form y' + P(x)y = Q(x) before reading off P(x). The student mistakenly set P(x) = 1 (the coefficient of y) instead of dividing by the leading coefficient 2x to isolate y'. This cascades through the entire integrating factor setup.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Leading coefficient omission is the #1 trap in first-order linear differential equations. A 25-minute spot-the-bug drill cements the mandatory standardization step.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.topic: Integration by Parts: Constant of Integration Omission
cases.question_text: Find the general antiderivative \int x e^x \, dx
canonical_steps: u = x, dv = e^x dx => du = dx, v = e^x
student_steps: u = x, dv = e^x dx => du = dx, v = e^x
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: All mathematical derivations, derivative computations, and integral evaluations were completely accurate. The only error was omitting the arbitrary constant of integration (+ C) for an indefinite integral, resulting in a mandatory 1-mark rubric penalty.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Rubric checklist hygiene. Takes only 10 minutes to train an automated end-of-solution verification habit, recovering up to 3 cumulative marks across an exam paper.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student multiplied individual derivatives (d/dx(x^3) * d/dx(sin(2x))) instead of applying the product rule (u'v + uv'). This fundamental algebraic misconception fails to distribute derivatives across multiplicative functions, leading to complete mark loss.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Product rule confusion is a foundational prerequisite leak. A 15-minute procedural flowchart visualizes the mandatory cross-multiplication pattern, locking in +4.0 marks.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: The student correctly executed the numerator cross-derivative subtraction ((1/x)(x^2) - 2x ln(x) = x - 2x ln(x)) but completely forgot to divide by the squared denominator v^2 = (x^2)^2 = x^4. Omitting the denominator loses 3 out of 5 marks under standard grading rubrics.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: The Two-Story House Foundation analogy (never build the second story without the ground slab) instills an automatic habit of writing v² first.

cases.subject: Linear Algebra
cases.topic: Matrix Determinant: 3x3 Cofactor Expansion Sign Flip
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student evaluated the 2x2 minor as (ad + bc) instead of (ad - bc), adding 10 + 12 = 22 instead of subtracting 10 - 12 = -2. This calculation sign flip in minor evaluation distorted the final determinant to 46 instead of 22.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Minor subtraction inversion is the most common procedural leak in linear algebra exams. Spot-the-bug drills with highlighted cross-arrows eliminate minor addition habits.

cases.subject: Linear Algebra
cases.question_text: If T: R^5 -> R^3 has dim(Ker(T)) = 2, find dim(Im(T)).
student_steps: T maps into R^3 so dim(Im(T)) must be 3 - 2 = 1
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student confused the dimension of the domain V (R^5) with the dimension of the codomain W (R^3). By substituting the codomain dimension 3 into Rank-Nullity (3 = 2 + dim(Im(T))), the student obtained 1 instead of 3. The Rank-Nullity Theorem strictly partitions the domain dimension dim(V), not the codomain.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: The Baggage Allowance Balance analogy clarifies that only departing luggage (domain dimension) can be split into lost vs arrived items.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.question_text: Find first 3 non-zero terms of Taylor series for ln(x) centered at a = 1
student_steps: f(0) is undefined so Taylor series cannot exist
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student confused a Maclaurin series (expansion centered at a = 0) with a general Taylor series centered at a = 1. While ln(0) is indeed undefined, the problem specifically specified the center a = 1 where ln(1) = 0 is well-defined and infinitely differentiable.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Taylor vs Maclaurin centering flowchart prevents the reflex assumption that all series expansions evaluate derivatives at zero.

cases.subject: Calculus III
canonical_steps: Test direct substitution: cos(0)/0 = 1/0 (determinate infinite limit, not 0/0)
Conclude limit does not exist (approaches -\infty from left, +\infty from right), L'Hopital rule does NOT apply
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student erroneously applied L'Hopital's Rule to a determinate form (1/0). L'Hopital requires indeterminate form 0/0 or inf/inf. Direct evaluation reveals vertical asymptote with two-sided divergence.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: L'Hopital gatekeeper condition drill stops students from taking derivatives automatically without checking the 0/0 condition.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student substituted dx correctly in Step 1, but squared the square-root denominator in Step 2: writing 4cos^2(theta) instead of sqrt(4cos^2(theta)) = 2cos(theta). This transformed a straightforward cancellation into an improper secant integral.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Radical simplification micro-drills reinforce Pythagorean identity transformations.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.topic: Partial Fraction Decomposition: Repeated Linear Factors
canonical_steps: Multiply by common denominator: 1 = A(x-1)^2 + Bx(x-1) + Cx
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student omitted the linear term B/(x-1) in the repeated factor decomposition template. For repeated linear factor (x-r)^2, the partial fraction template must include ascending powers from 1 to the multiplicity.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Partial fraction template decision tree ensures complete denominator multiplicity coverage.

cases.subject: Physics / Vector Calculus
cases.question_text: Check if F = <2xy, x^2 + z, y> is conservative
canonical_steps: Compute curl(F) = <dF3/dy - dF2/dz, dF1/dz - dF3/dx, dF2/dx - dF1/dy>
Since curl is zero everywhere on simply connected domain, F is conservative
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Fully satisfied derivation. Student correctly set up the cross product determinant for curl, calculated partial derivatives with zero errors, and deduced that the vector field is conservative.

recovery_recommendation.rationale: Full marks achieved. Retain mastery through spaced repetition.

cases.subject: Calculus III
cases.topic: Definite Integral: Sign Flip on Bounds Inversion
cases.forensic_leak_analysis: Student inverted the evaluation order: substituting the lower bound first instead of upper bound F(b) - F(a). When evaluating \int_a^b, the formula is strictly F(b) - F(a).

recovery_recommendation.rationale: The Odometer Analogy (end reading minus start reading) eliminates the habit of subtracting the smaller number from the larger number.
